explanation: Searched Mathlib for any statement identifying the stabilizer of the class of `1` in a quotient module with the set of units congruent to `1` modulo the ideal. Greps for `stabilizer` together with `Quotient.mk 1`/`(1 : R)`, for `principalUnit`/`PrincipalUnit`, for `(u : R) - 1 ∈ I` and similar patterns, and for related stabilizer lemmas in `Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/*`, `Mathlib/RingTheory/Invariant/*` and `Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Quotient/*` found only unrelated results (`ValuationSubring.principalUnitGroup`, `Ideal.Quotient.stabilizerHom`, `Ideal.inertia_le_stabilizer`, `MulAction.stabilizer ... ⧸ H`). The closest Mathlib facts are the generic `Submodule.Quotient.eq` (`mk x = mk y ↔ x - y ∈ p`) and `Ideal.Quotient.mk_eq_one_iff_sub_mem` (which needs `[I.IsTwoSided]` and concerns the ring quotient map, not the unit action's stabilizer), so the theorem is not a statement present in Mathlib nor an instantiation of a single Mathlib declaration: deriving it needs the group-action rewriting (`MulAction.mem_stabilizer_iff`, `Submodule.Quotient.mk_smul`, `Units.smul_def`) in addition to the quotient equality, exactly what the library's own proof does.
